title: feat(spec,automation,app-shell): a read-only record_link screen field shows a record the run created, by its display name, as a link to its record page
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9VyLmRWa1EMU9YudB6tnf1C)_

Fixes #26304
Fixes #25872

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added

## Summary

A screen flow that creates records can now end on a result screen that links them. This is ruling B on #25872 (6422899013) and the contract card #26304, landed in one PR across spec, engine and console, in the shape of the `file` screen field (#26134).

```ts
{ id: 'done', type: 'screen', config: { title: 'Lead converted', fields: [
  { name: 'account_link', label: 'Account', type: 'record_link',
    reference: 'crm_account', defaultValue: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'account.id' } },
  { name: 'contact_link', label: 'Contact', type: 'record_link',
    reference: 'crm_contact', defaultValue: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'contact.id' } },
] } },
```

- **Spec.** `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` gains the `type` member `'record_link'`. `reference` and `defaultValue` are required on it, and `required`, `options`, `placeholder`, `min` and `max` are refused, each at its own key. Every other `type` value parses exactly as before.
- **Engine.** `validateScreenInputs` refuses any value sent under a `record_link` field's name (`null` included, visible or hidden) with `invalid_value` inside `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT`. The value is never bound to a flow variable, and the refusal keeps the pause. `judgeHeadlessScreen` never counts a `record_link` field as answered by a caller, so a result screen always pauses.
- **Console.** `ScreenFieldInput` gets a `record_link` branch. It shows the record's display name through `LookupField`'s `readonly` branch (which fetches the record and names it from the referenced object's schema, ADR-0079 `nameField`), inside a router `Link` to `/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID` built by `appRecordPath`, the builder the record page's related lists use. An empty id draws the platform's "—" with no link. An object the console cannot route to, or a mount with no router, shows the name without a link. `visibleWhen` works as on any field. `initialScreenValues` never seeds the field and `screenResumeValues` strips it, so the dialog never posts it.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` gains "A read-only record link", and the resume-contract list names the new refusal. The designer form's `reference` column now reads "Target object" and describes both `lookup` and `record_link`.

## The member's name: `record_link`, not `record`

The ruling let the dev propose the name and suggested `record`. A screen field's `type` borrows the object field vocabulary (`text`, `number`, `lookup`, `file`, and so on), and `FieldType` already has `'record'` for a name-keyed map of embedded sub-objects (`field.zod.ts`, ADR-0007). One word with two meanings in one field vocabulary is a trap for an author, so the member is `record_link`, snake_case like `master_detail`. The name lives in one exported constant, `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_TYPE`, which the engine and the console both import.

## For the contract review: final shape and refusal texts

Shape: no new key. `type` stays `z.string().optional()`. The rule is a branch of the existing `superRefine` on `ScreenFieldConfigSchema`, taken when `type === 'record_link'` (exact match). It adds one issue per broken rule, each with `code: 'custom'`, and returns before the lookup rule. `.shape` still lists the same keys.

| Path | When | Message |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `reference` | absent, empty or blank | `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_REFERENCE_REQUIRED`: "A `type: 'record_link'` screen field must declare `reference` — the name of the object the record belongs to (e.g. `reference: 'crm_account'`). Without it the field cannot name the record or link to its page." |
| `defaultValue` | absent or `null` | `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_DEFAULT_VALUE_REQUIRED`: "A `type: 'record_link'` screen field must declare `defaultValue` — the id of the record it shows, usually a CEL value envelope over a flow variable (e.g. `defaultValue: { dialect: 'cel', source: 'account_id' }`). The field takes no input, so without it there is never a record to show." |
| `required`, `options`, `placeholder`, `min`, `max` | present, with any value (`required: false` too) | `screenFieldRecordLinkRefusedKey(KEY)`: "A `type: 'record_link'` screen field shows a record and takes no input, so it cannot declare `KEY`: the run refuses any value submitted under its name. Remove the key, or use a `lookup` field to let the user pick a record." |
| resume bag, field `NAME` | the key is present, any value | `invalid_value`: "Screen field "NAME" shows a record and takes no value — leave it out of the resume", inside the `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` envelope with the declared field list |

New exports from `@objectstack/spec/automation` (api-surface and export-origins regenerated): `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_TYPE`, `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_REFERENCE_REQUIRED`, `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_DEFAULT_VALUE_REQUIRED`, `SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_REFUSED_KEYS`, `screenFieldRecordLinkRefusedKey`. The `ScreenFieldSpec` wire contract only gains docblock text. No new `FieldErrorCode` member: `invalid_value` is the catalog's "rejected for a reason no other member names".

## Tests

Measured on this branch.

- `@objectstack/spec`: `screen-field-record-link.test.ts` (new, 9 tests) covers the accepted shapes (envelope id, literal id, help text, `visibleWhen`), each required key refused at its path, each refused key refused at its path (including `required: false`), several broken rules reported together, the refusal through `ScreenConfigSchema`, other types untouched (including `record`), and no tracker id in any refusal text. Full package: Test Files 805 passed (805), Tests 23263 passed, 1 todo.
- `@objectstack/service-automation`: `screen-input-record-link-field.test.ts` (new, 6 tests) covers no value accepted, any value refused (`null`, empty, the shown id, another id, an object, `0`, `false`), refused while hidden, exact-member matching, and the headless verdict with a positive control. `builtin/screen-record-link-resume.test.ts` (new, 2 tests) runs the engine: two `create_record` nodes, then a result screen whose two links arrive typed `record_link` with `reference` and the created ids; a resume carrying a link's value is refused with nothing run after the screen; the clean resume completes. The account link is named `account`, after the very variable its id comes from, so a bound refused value would have broken the audit write after the screen. Full package: Test Files 209 passed (209), Tests 2707 passed (2707).
- `@object-ui/app-shell`: `FlowRunner.recordLink-25872.test.tsx` (new, 6 tests) renders the real `FlowRunner` and the real `LookupField` over a fake data source whose objects name records by `company_name` / `full_name`, not `name`. It covers two links with the right names and hrefs; "—" and no link for an empty id; an unroutable object and a router-less mount showing the name unlinked; `visibleWhen`; Submit posting only the real input; and the seed/strip helpers. With the neighbours `views/__tests__/FlowRunner*`, `metadata-admin/previews/` and `spec-symbol-parity`: Test Files 160 passed (160), Tests 1794 passed (1794). The full app-shell suite is left to CI `Test UI`.
- Dogfood: `flow-screen-record-link.dogfood.test.ts` (new) boots a real stack and drives the trigger and resume doors. The run creates an account and a contact and pauses on the result screen. Both fields arrive as `record_link` with their objects and the ids of the records this run wrote, and each id reads back through `/data/OBJECT/ID` with its `nameField` value (what the console shows). A resume carrying `account_link` or `contact_link: null` is refused `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` naming the field, and the clean resume completes the run. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run test/flow-screen-record-link.dogfood.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 2 passed (2). The full battery is not owed: no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm.
- Type-check: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/dogfood` `typecheck`, and `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check`, exit 0 each.
- Console: `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/console` on the merge head `a2c646635b`, exit 0.

## Ablation

Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which restored the file to its HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty.

- Spec: `if (field.type === SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_TYPE) {` to `if (false as boolean) {` turned 5 of 9 tests red.
- Engine: deleting the two guard lines of the `record_link` resume pass (so it skips every field) turned 3 tests red across both new files.
- Engine: removing the `record_link` skip in `judgeHeadlessScreen` turned 1 test red. A first attempt used a replacement that was a substring of its anchor, and the tool refused it before any run; that attempt was void and was redone with a distinct replacement.
- Console: `if (isRecordLinkScreenField(field)) {` to `if (false as boolean) {` in `ScreenFieldInput` turned 5 of 6 tests red.
- Console: removing the skip in `initialScreenValues` turned 1 test red. The Submit test stayed green under that mutation because `screenResumeValues` still strips the key, which is the intended second layer.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `27c90bb39d` (115 commands; the same list as at the earlier `582dd2f9`). Each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe, and `--ran` reconciled them: "115 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 114 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED". The 114 that ran exited 0. They include `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-empty-changeset`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:export-origins`, `check:docs`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check-sdui-manifest` (no record moves), `check:nul-bytes` and `check:liveness`.

After merging `origin/main` (12 commits, none touching this diff's files) the spec was rebuilt and the ratchet families re-ran on the merge head `a2c646635b`: `check:generated` exit 0, and `check:type-check-debt` exit 0 ("0 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number"). `check:skill-examples` and the `check-plugin-teardown-shape` self-test first stopped on missing prerequisites (an unbuilt `client-react` and a shallow clone); both re-ran after the prerequisite was met and exited 0. `pnpm --dir ui run check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.

Not measured locally, left to CI: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which needs a full workspace `pnpm build` and stopped on that prerequisite with exit 3 before reading anything. This diff does not change any package's build shape.

## Acceptance notes

- **Widening, as declared.** Before this PR `type` was an open string, so `type: 'record_link'` with any keys parsed and rendered a text input. It now refuses a `record_link` field without `reference` or `defaultValue`, or with an input key. No producer of a `record_link` screen field exists in this repository (`git grep` over `examples/`, `packages/` and `ui/` source finds none), so nothing that parses today is refused. The claim's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is kept.
- **The result screen still ends with Submit.** As the ruling's analysis said, a user who follows a link before submitting leaves the run paused, as closing the dialog does. Whether the dialog stays open across that navigation depends on the host page; this PR does not change it.
- **A record that cannot be read** (deleted, or denied to the user) settles `LookupField`'s readonly branch on "—", and the link around it still points at the record page, which then answers for itself. The name is never replaced with the raw id.
- **Case.** The console reads `record_link` exactly, as the spec and engine do, unlike `file` and `number`, which the console lowercases. A field declared `type: 'Record_Link'` is an ordinary text input on every layer.
- **Skill and eval are a follow-up.** The skills surface is governed, so the owed skill text and eval prompt (#26184) are in #26347 (`skills/objectstack-automation`, an entry in `evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json`). This PR does not touch `skills/**`.
- After a published `@objectstack/*` release carries this, the hotcrm seat can lift hotcrm#2285's `Blocked-by:`.
